The Prophet said the best people are his generation, then the next, then the next, after whom come people who testify unasked, break vows, are untrustworthy and grow fat.
The Prophet said none then living on earth would survive a hundred years, and swore to it when asked about the Hour, whose knowledge he said is with Allah.
The Prophet forbade reviling his Companions, saying others spending gold as much as Uhud would not equal a mudd of theirs, after Khalid b. Walid reviled Abd al-Rahman b. Awf.
The Prophet foretold Uwais of Qaran, kind to his mother and cured of leprosy but a spot, and Umar found him and asked him to seek forgiveness for him.
Foretelling the conquest of Egypt, the Prophet urged good treatment of its people for kinship's sake and leaving when two disputed a brick's space, which Abu Dharr later did.
A man the Prophet sent to an Arab tribe was reviled and beaten, and the Prophet said the people of Oman would neither have reviled nor beaten him.
Ibn Umar praised the dead Abdullah b. Zubair hanging by the road; his mother Asma told Hajjaj he had ruined his own Hereafter and was the foretold murderer of Thaqif.
The Prophet said a man of Persia would reach faith even at the Pleiades, placing his hand on Salman when asked about a verse of Surah al-Jumu'a.
The Prophet said people are like a hundred camels, among which not even one is found fit for riding.
The Prophet named the mother three times as most deserving of good treatment, then the father and nearest relatives, and sent back a man seeking jihad to serve his parents.
Ignoring his mother's calls while praying, Juraij was accused of fathering a child as she had prayed, and the infant, one of three who spoke in the cradle, cleared him.
The Prophet said humbled is one whose parents reach old age yet he does not enter Paradise, and the finest goodness is kindness to one's father's loved ones.
The Prophet said virtue is a kind disposition, and vice is what rankles in the heart and what one dislikes people to know.
Allah joins whoever joins kinship and severs the severer, who will not enter Paradise; joining it widens provision and lengthens life, and kindness to harsh relatives brings Allah's help.
The Prophet forbade hatred, envy and enmity among Muslims and keeping away from a brother for more than three days, the better of the two being the first to greet.
The Prophet forbade suspicion, spying, envy, malice and outbidding, called Muslims brothers whose blood, wealth and honour are inviolable, and said Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not faces.
Every Monday and Thursday Allah forgives every servant who associates nothing with Him, except two who bear rancour against each other, who are held back until they reconcile.
Allah will shade on Resurrection Day those who love each other for Him, and an angel told a man visiting his brother for Allah's sake that Allah loves him.
Visiting the sick keeps one in Paradise's fruit garden until he returns, and on Resurrection Day Allah will reproach man for not visiting, feeding or giving drink to His servants.
The Prophet's own fever was severe, and he said a believer's every hardship, even a thorn's prick, wipes away sins, promising Paradise to a woman with falling sickness who endured.
Allah says He forbade oppression, bids His servants seek guidance, food, clothing and forgiveness from Him, cannot be harmed or benefited by them, and repays their recorded deeds.
Oppression is darkness on Resurrection Day, when the wrongdoer pays victims with his good deeds and even a hornless sheep gets its right; Allah respites the oppressor, then seizes him.
When an emigrant and an Ansari called on their groups, the Prophet condemned cries of ignorance and said to help a brother, wrongdoer or wronged; believers are like one body.
When two people abuse each other, the sin falls on the one who began, as long as the wronged one does not go beyond the limit.
The Prophet said charity does not lessen wealth, Allah raises in honour whoever forgives, and raises in rank whoever humbles himself for Allah's sake.
Backbiting is saying of a brother what he dislikes, and if untrue it is slander; Allah will cover on Resurrection Day the faults of a servant who covers others' faults.
The Prophet spoke kindly even to a man he called bad, and said Allah is kind and loves kindness, which adorns all things, and one denied it is denied good.
The Prophet had a cursed camel unloaded and set loose, said cursers are neither intercessors nor witnesses on Resurrection Day, and that he was sent as mercy, not to curse.
Being human, the Prophet asked Allah that any curse, rebuke or blow he gave a Muslim become purification and nearness to Allah, as he told Aisha and Umm Sulaim.
Sent twice by the Prophet to call Mu'awiya, the boy Ibn Abbas found him eating each time, and the Prophet said, May Allah not fill his belly.
The Prophet said the worst of people is the double-faced one, who comes to some people with one face and to others with another.
One who reconciles people by saying good is not a liar, and Ibn Shihab knew of falsehood being allowed only in war, reconciliation, and words between husband and wife.
The Prophet said truth leads to virtue and Paradise and lying to obscenity and Hell till one is recorded truthful or liar, and defined slander as tale-carrying that divides people.
The strong man controls himself in rage rather than wrestling well, and the Prophet said seeking refuge with Allah from Satan would end an angry man's fit.
When Allah shaped Adam in Paradise, Iblis went round him and, finding him hollow, knew he was created unable to control himself.
The Prophet said whoever fights his brother should avoid striking the face, for Allah created Adam in His image.
Seeing people in Syria held in the sun over revenue or jizya, Hisham b. Hakim quoted the Prophet that Allah will torment those who torment people, and they were freed.
Arrows carried in the mosque or market must be held by their heads so no Muslim is hurt, and angels curse whoever points a weapon at his brother.
A man who removed a thorny branch or harmful tree from a path was forgiven and entered Paradise, and the Prophet told Abu Barza to remove harmful things from paths.
A woman entered Hell because of a cat she tied up until it died, neither feeding nor giving it water nor letting it eat the vermin of the earth.
